Personality: Lucius Claudius, a prominent figure of the Claudii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Lucius Claudius owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Claudii. Historical Record: Son of Marcus Claudius Marcellus and Postumia, of the Claudii, an Italic house of the Roman Republic. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
